/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 03 August 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2843 (111)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4564 (268)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2135 (48)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1610 (1)
Baltic Handysize Index: 884 (-3)
CAPESIZE
The market began the week on a solid footing, extending Friday’s positive momentum and finishing with another strong round of gains. The BCI 5TC advanced by $2,435 to $41,395, with strength evident across both basins. In the Pacific, sentiment continued to improve as owners maintained a firm stance. While only two major miners were active on C5, operator demand remained healthy and increasing owner resistance helped push rates steadily higher throughout the day. Initial bids around $13.50 quickly moved to $14.00 and into the low-$14s as owners withdrew offers, with many now targeting $15.00. Reports circulated of business concluded above $14.00, although these remained unconfirmed by the close. The C5 index reflected the stronger tone, rising by $1.395 to $14.445. Attention is also beginning to shift towards the approaching Tropical Storm Dolphin. Although landfall is still several days away, precautionary measures are already being implemented, with market participants closely monitoring the potential impact on vessel movements and port operations later this week. The Atlantic maintained its recent positive trajectory, with South Atlantic and West Africa continuing to underpin improvements on C3. While the last confirmed fixture remained at $34.25, charterers were already indicating around $34.50 against owner expectations closer to $35.50, highlighting the widening gap as owners sought to build on the improving sentiment. The C3 index gained $0.650 to settle at $34.810.
PANAMAX
A quieter start to the week saw market fundamentals across both basins remain largely unchanged from last week. Brokers reported that available tonnage in both the North Continent and Western Mediterranean continues to be tight. As a result, Charterers seeking cover for trans-Atlantic and fronthaul voyages are being forced to increase their bid levels in an attempt to attract Owner interest. Several market participants also noted that, with prompt vessel availability limited and sentiment remaining firm, Owners are showing little urgency to engage or even indicate workable fixing levels. In the Pacific, positive sentiment continues to build, supported by increased mineral demand alongside grain exports from the North Pacific, although activity is said to be relatively quiet today. Brokers noted that while the overall tonnage count remains healthy, the prospect of weather-related disruptions in the coming days could tighten local vessel supply in certain areas. As a result, Owners may find pockets of opportunity emerging as Charterers seek replacement tonnage to maintain loading schedules, potentially providing additional support to freight levels across the basin.
SUPRAMAX
A typical Monday of collecting and catching up with what was concluded at the end of last week. The North American routes again showed positive returns, with most of the remainder of the routes relatively flat, the 11TC average was up $11 to settle at $20,347. The South Atlantic continued to ease with a shortage of fresh enquiry, whilst the Continent and Mediterranean seemed flat. In the East there was little new information with sentiment remaining negative with the growing tonnage list slowly eroding rate levels.

Atlantic
The Captain Sitaras (60,900 2022) prompt Port Said was said to be on subjects for a trip via Abu Qir redelivery Houston intention bulk cement with Sofon at $19,000 plus $200,000 lumpsum ilohc and the Elina B (58,551 2011) prompt Diliskelesi fixed a trip via Novorossiysk intention grains redelivery Bangladesh-Japan range (intention SE Asia) at something in the mid $30,000’s.

Asia
A 54k open Lianyungang early Aug fixed in the high $19,000's maybe $20,000 for a steels cargo to Karachi, the Jabal Harim (63,277 2016) Port Qasim 3-6 August fixed 2 to 3 laden legs at around $20,500 (1st leg Salalah/Madagascar with limestone) to Norden and the Cumbria (61,268 2015) Hazira 8-14 August fixed a trip via Pakistan redelivery US Gulf intention bagged cement at around $12,000 with a split rate after 70 days with Ultrabulk. The Dubai Sun (61,344 2010) Bedi 30 July fixed a trip via Karachi redelivery Hambantota at $20,000 with Inmar, the Bahri Haya (63,498 2017) Fujairah 2-3 August has fixed a trip via Oman redelivery WC India with aggregates at $23,000 with unnamed Charterers and the Centurion Romulus (64,618 2025) prompt Kandla fixed an aggregates cargo to Chittagong at $20,000 with Guardian Bulk being linked as Charterers, although another source suggested it was Teambulk.
HANDYSIZE
Although last week ended on a quiet note, there seemed a decent amount of rumoured trades today, although some may have been concluded several days ago. The BHSI was down 3 at 884 and the HS7TC average lost $63 to settle at $15,906, with every route negative, although negligible amounts on many. Sentiment in both Basins remains fairly negative, and with the onset of the Summer holidays, it remains a concern were the fresh impetus will come from in the short term. The Prime Star (36,570 2012) Oran 1-3 August was said to have fixed short period redelivery Atlantic basis delivery Garrucha at $14,000, but the Charterer was not disclosed.

Atlantic
A handy was rumoured to have fixed delivery Barcelona for a trip Recalada at $7,000 with Dead Sea Works, a 40k-dwt was reported fixed delivery Nemrut for a trip with steels to WC South America in the $17,000’s and a 35k-dwt fixed basis Canakkale via CVB redelivery West Mediterranean at $10,000, but the Charterer was not reported.

Asia
A 32k-dwt open Singapore was said to have clean fixed for legs in the mid/high $15,000’s, however further details were lacking, and a 38k-dwt open Thailand fixed a trip Japan with woodpellets at $14,500. Further North a 37k-dwt open North China was reported fixed for a trip to SE Asia with redelivery Singapore at $17,000 and a 36k-dwt open CJK agreed $17,400 for a trip to Indonesia intention steels.

ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场在8月第一周呈现分化格局，好望角型船领涨全市，BCI 5TC大涨$2,435至$41,395，太平洋和大西洋市场同步走强；巴拿马型船受限于运力紧张，租金稳步上扬；超灵便型基本持平，灵便型小跌。热带风暴Dolphin逼近中国，可能加剧港口拥堵并影响短期运价，需密切关注。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: 好望角型船成为市场领头羊，太平洋C5指数单日跳涨$1.395至$14.445，大西洋C3升至$34.810。巴拿马型船运力趋紧，北欧和西地中海可用船舶有限，租家被迫抬价。超灵便型船表现平淡，灵便型船逆势走弱，为唯一下跌板块。FFA市场显示8月合约强劲，Cape期货曲线受太平洋市场走强提振。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 好望角型船市场情绪显著改善，太平洋初始报价从$13.50迅速攀升至$14以上，多家船东瞄准$15目标。大西洋市场租家报价$34.50而船东期望$35.50，分歧扩大。巴拿马型船太平洋市场受矿物需求增加和粮食出口支撑，情绪向好。灵便型船受夏季假期影响，短期内恐难获新动能。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 重点关注热带风暴Dolphin动态，其可能在中国港口引发预防性措施，造成船舶积压，利好即期运价。太平洋好望角型船C5航线为当前最强信号，C3大西洋航线存在补涨空间。巴拿马型船北大陆和西地中海运力紧张状况或将延续至8月中旬。

market_watch: 热带风暴Dolphin正在逼近中国，港口预防措施可能加剧船舶拥堵并支撑即期运价
Fortescue二季度发货量同比下降2.5Mt至52.7Mt，关注后续铁矿贸易流向变化
Cape FFA 8月合约大幅上涨至38,350，Aug-Sep价差收窄至-500，显示短期看涨情绪浓厚

route_focus.view: 大西洋市场维持强势，C3指数涨$0.650至$34.810，租家报价$34.50与船东期望$35.50存在差距，短期仍有上行动能，建议关注南大西洋和西非方向货盘。
巴拿马型船北大陆和西地中海运力持续紧张，租家被迫抬价觅船，预期短期租金稳中有升，关注北大西洋和fronthaul航线机会。
灵便型船HS1航线（Skaw-Passero至Rio de Janeiro-Recalada）报$8,564，下跌$40，为近期弱势代表，受夏季假期和情绪低迷拖累，短期难有起色。
